candidates.text: In China's ancient Book of Rites, 50 is when ‘he is getting grey’ and ‘can discharge all the duties of an officer’.

source.label: James Legge (trans.), The Li Ki, Book I: Khü Lî, Part I (Sacred Books of the East vol. 27, 1885), Internet Sacred Text Archive

candidates.evidence: When he is fifty, we say, 'He is getting grey;' he can discharge all the duties of an officer.
candidates.check: Legge's translation of the Book of Rites (Liji), chapter Qu Li I, which names each decade of life (forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty or ninety). The line is specifically about age fifty. Different text from the Analects lines used at 40 and 60. Minor overlap in theme with the grey-hair survey at 54.

candidates.text: From 50, US workers may make extra ‘catch-up contributions’ to retirement plans such as a 401(k), up to $8,000 a year in 2026.

source.label: Internal Revenue Service (US), Retirement topics: Catch-up contributions

candidates.evidence: Individuals who are age 50 or over at the end of the calendar year can make annual catch-up contributions. Annual catch-up contributions up to $8,000 in 2026 may be permitted by these plans: 401(k) (other than a SIMPLE 401(k)) 403(b) SARSEP governmental 457(b)
candidates.check: US federal tax rule: the entitlement begins at age 50 ("age 50 or over at the end of the calendar year"). Dollar limit is the 2026 figure stated on the IRS page, fetched Sept 2026.

candidates.text: In 2024, the median age of registered nurses in the United States was 50, up from 46 in 2022.

source.label: National Council of State Boards of Nursing, 2024 National Nursing Workforce Survey (infographic)

candidates.evidence: The median age of RNs was 50 in 2024, increasing from a median age of 46 in 2022
candidates.check: Median age of US registered nurses, 2024 survey (published in Journal of Nursing Regulation 16(1), 2025) = 50. Note: the 2020 survey gave 52 (offered at age 52); use only one of the two.

candidates.text: In the United States, men become grandfathers at a median age of 52, according to a 2015 study comparing 25 countries.

source.label: Leopold & Skopek, 'The Demography of Grandparenthood: An International Profile', Social Forces 94(2), 2015

candidates.evidence: we analyzed retrospective data from the United States (NSFH) and 24 European countries (GGS, ESS, DEAS). ... Compared to the United States (49 years among women, 52 years among men), grandparenthood in Eastern Europe occurs up to three years earlier in life; in Western Europe, up to eight years later.
candidates.check: Median age at grandparenthood, US men = 52 (US plus 24 European countries = 25). OUP returned 403 to curl; abstract read via WebFetch, and it matches the wording confirmed by curl in the earlier round. Same study as the fact at 49 (US women), so the two read as a pair.

candidates.text: In 2020, the median age of registered nurses in the United States was 52, up from 51 in 2017.

source.label: National Council of State Boards of Nursing, The 2020 National Nursing Workforce Survey, Journal of Nursing Regulation 12(1) Supplement, April 2021

candidates.evidence: Aging of the Workforce The median age of RNs was 52 years, up from 51 years in 2017.
candidates.check: Median age of US RNs in the 2020 survey = 52. Dated: later NCSBN surveys give 46 (2022) and 50 (2024), so the text is in the past tense with its year. Do not use together with the 2024 nurses candidate at 50.

candidates.text: The average age of US Representatives at the start of the 119th Congress, in January 2025, was 57.9 years.

source.label: Congressional Research Service, Membership of the 119th Congress: A Profile (R48535), 2025, via EveryCRSReport.com

candidates.evidence: The average age of Members of the House at the beginning of the 119th Congress was 57.9 years; of Senators, 63.9 years.
candidates.check: 119th Congress began 3 January 2025 (report text: 'at the beginning of the 119th Congress (January 3, 2025)'). An average of 57.9 years means the typical member is 57 in completed years. congress.gov returned 403, so the CRS text was read on the EveryCRSReport mirror.

candidates.text: In England in 2021, women aged 55 to 59 were more likely than any other group to give unpaid care to someone: 19.9% of them did.

source.label: Office for National Statistics, Unpaid care by age, sex and deprivation, England and Wales: Census 2021

candidates.evidence: In England, females aged between 55 to 59 years provided the most unpaid care (19.9%), while females aged between 5 to 17 years were least likely to provide unpaid care (1.5%).
candidates.check: Census 2021, England, females aged 55-59 = highest share of any age-sex group. 57 is the centre of the 55-59 band.

candidates.text: In the United States, 73 is the age at which savers must generally start taking ‘required minimum distributions’ from IRAs and retirement plans.

source.label: Internal Revenue Service (US), Retirement plan and IRA required minimum distributions FAQs

candidates.evidence: Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) are minimum amounts that IRA and retirement plan account owners generally must withdraw annually starting with the year they reach age 73.
candidates.check: US federal rule; the threshold age is exactly 73. (Workplace-plan participants who are still working may delay; 'generally' in the text covers this.)

candidates.text: Japan counted about 1.71 million people aged 73 in October 2024, more than twice its 716,000 babies under one year old.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates as of 1 October 2024, Table 1 (population by single year of age)

candidates.check: Official single-year estimates for Japan, 1 October 2024, in thousands: age 73 = 1,710 thousand; age 0 = 716 thousand (ratio 2.4). Weaker, count-type candidate.

candidates.text: Since July 2022, Canada's Old Age Security pension has been 10% higher from the month after a person turns 75.

source.label: Old Age Security Act (Canada), s. 7(5), Justice Laws Website

candidates.evidence: Full monthly pension — persons aged 75 years or older (5) Beginning in the payment quarter commencing on July 1, 2022, for the period that begins in the month after the month in which a person attains 75 years of age, the amount of the full monthly pension, as it is calculated in accordance with subsections (1) to (4), is increased by 10%.
candidates.check: Canadian federal law; the increase is tied to attaining 75. (canada.ca would not load via curl; the statute itself was fetched instead. A WebFetch of canada.ca's OAS payments page agreed: 'In July 2022, the Old Age Security pension was permanently increased by 10% for seniors aged 75 and over.')

candidates.text: In Japan in 2024, the 20.78 million people aged 75 and over outnumbered those aged 65 to 74.

source.label: Cabinet Office of Japan, Annual Report on the Ageing Society FY2025 (English summary)

candidates.evidence: The number of the population aged 65-74 is 15.47 million, accounting for 12.5% of the total population. The population aged 75 and over is 20.78 million, accounting for 16.8% of the total population, and has overtaken the population aged 65-74 in size.
candidates.check: Figures as of 1 October 2024 (report text: 'as of October 1, 2024'). 75 is the defining lower edge of the 75-and-over group.

candidates.text: In Japan, 77 is kiju, named for the character 喜, joy, which in cursive script looks like 七十七, the numerals for seventy-seven.

source.label: The Japan Times, 28 Dec 2025

candidates.evidence: After 還暦 we have 喜寿 (kiju, the 77th birthday), whose name comes from the character 喜 (yorokobu, joy). In 草書体 (sōshotai, cursive script), the kanji appears as 㐂, resembling a stylized form of 七十七 (nana-jū-nana, 7-10-7).
candidates.check: Kiju is explicitly 'the 77th birthday'. Same pattern as sotsuju at 90. The rest of the article is paywalled, but this passage is on the public part. Nippon.com (Japan Data, 5 Jan 2024) confirms: '喜寿 ( Kiju , 77 years old)'.

candidates.text: In Japan's 2024 population pyramid, 77 is the oldest age of the post-war baby boom: people born from 1947 to 1949 were then 75 to 77.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates as of 1 October 2024, Table 1 (population by single year of age), Figure 2 (population pyramid)

candidates.evidence: 図２ 我が国の人口ピラミッド（2024年10月１日現在） ... 75～77歳： 1947年～1949年の 第１次ベビーブーム
candidates.check: Pyramid annotation, Japan, 1 October 2024: 'Ages 75-77: the first baby boom of 1947-1949'. 77 is the upper edge of that named range. Table 1 in the same PDF: age 77 = 1,784 thousand.

candidates.text: Japan's population pyramid dips at 78: in 2024 there were 1.09 million people that age but 1.78 million aged 77, a trace of the fall in births around 1945.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates as of 1 October 2024, Table 1 (population by single year of age) and Figure 2 (population pyramid)

candidates.check: Japan, 1 October 2024. Pyramid annotation: 'Ages 78, 79: the fall in births around the end of the Second World War (1945)'. Table 1 (thousands): age 77 = 1,784, age 78 = 1,088. Both in the same Statistics Bureau PDF.

candidates.text: Worldwide, about 29 million people were aged 78 in 2025, according to United Nations population projections.

source.label: United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024, population by single age, medium variant 2024-2100 (CSV)

candidates.check: Row for World, 2025, age 78 (thousands): total 28,736.8 thousand, rounded to about 29 million. Medium-variant projection (the file covers 2024-2100), so the text says 'projections'. Fallback only.

candidates.text: In September 2023, for the first time, one person in ten in Japan was aged 80 or over.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Statistical Topics No. 138: The Elderly in Japan (Respect for the Aged Day), 17 Sept 2023

candidates.evidence: 80歳以上人口は1259万人で、前年に比べ27万人増 ... 80歳以上人口は10.1％ ... 80歳以上人口は、総人口に占める割合が初めて10％を超え、10人に１人が80歳以上となっています。
candidates.check: Japan, estimate as of 15 September 2023: people aged 80+ = 12.59 million, 10.1% of the population. The text says the share went over 10% for the first time: 'one in ten people is 80 or over'. 80 is the defining edge. The 2026 edition (No. 149) gives 12.88 million, 10.5%.

candidates.text: Catholic cardinals who have reached their 80th birthday do not vote in the conclave that elects a new pope.

source.label: John Paul II, Apostolic Constitution Universi Dominici Gregis (1996), Vatican

candidates.evidence: The right to elect the Roman Pontiff belongs exclusively to the Cardinals of Holy Roman Church, with the exception of those who have reached their eightieth birthday before the day of the Roman Pontiff's death or the day when the Apostolic See becomes vacant.
candidates.check: Church law, no. 33. The age limit is exactly the 80th birthday. The preamble notes the rule was kept from Paul VI.

candidates.text: In Japan, 80 is sanju, because the abbreviated form of the character 傘, written 仐, looks like 八十, the numerals for 80.

source.label: Nippon.com, Japanese Names for Age Milestones from 60 to 100, 5 Jan 2024

candidates.evidence: 傘寿 ( Sanju , 80 years old) The abbreviated kanji for 傘 is 仐, which looks like 八十 ( hachijū ), or the number 80 written in characters.
candidates.check: Traditional Japanese milestone name for exactly 80. Worded in parallel with the sotsuju fact at 90.

candidates.text: Some Jewish men celebrate a second bar mitzvah at 83, having lived a life span of 70 years since the first, at 13.

source.label: My Jewish Learning, The Adult Bar/Bat Mitzvah

candidates.evidence: Most descriptions of an adult bar or bat mitzvah tend to focus on people of a certain age: women old enough to have grown up when females had no ritual purpose on the bimah (pulpit) of any synagogue and 83-year-old men who celebrate a second bar mitzvah, having lived a life span of 70 years since the first.
candidates.check: Custom tied to exactly 83 (13 + 70). The same page states 'by Jewish law, a boy reaches adulthood when he turns 13'. Different angle from the fact at 113 (a first bar mitzvah held 100 years late).

candidates.text: Japan counted about 1.19 million people aged 83 in October 2024, well over its 716,000 babies under one year old.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates as of 1 October 2024, Table 1 (population by single year of age)

candidates.check: Official single-year estimates for Japan, 1 October 2024 (thousands): age 83 = 1,191; age 0 = 716. Count-type fallback.

candidates.text: Under US health-privacy rules, 89 is the oldest age that may appear in de-identified records; anyone older is grouped as ‘90 or older’.

source.label: 45 CFR 164.514(b)(2) (HIPAA Privacy Rule, 'safe harbor' de-identification), Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School

candidates.evidence: (i) The following identifiers of the individual or of relatives, employers, or household members of the individual, are removed: ... (C) All elements of dates (except year) for dates directly related to an individual, including birth date, admission date, discharge date, date of death; and all ages over 89 and all elements of dates (including year) indicative of such age, except that such ages and elements may be aggregated into a single category of age 90 or older;
candidates.check: US federal regulation: ages over 89 must be removed or grouped as '90 or older', so 89 is the highest age that can be stated. The same text was also fetched from the eCFR renderer (ecfr.gov). HHS's own guidance page returned 403.

candidates.text: In Japan in October 2024, 437,000 women and 220,000 men were aged 89, about two women for every man.

source.label: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates as of 1 October 2024, Table 1 (population by single year of age)

candidates.check: Official single-year estimates for Japan, 1 October 2024 (thousands): age 89 total 657, men 220, women 437; sex ratio 50.3 men per 100 women (注: 女性100人に対する男性の数). A count, not a survival statistic, but it reflects one; use with care.

candidates.text: Korean has a word for age 91: mangbaek (望百), ‘looking toward a hundred’.

source.label: National Institute of Korean Language, Standard Korean Language Dictionary, entry 망백

candidates.evidence: 망백 (望百) 「명사」 백(百)을 바라본다는 뜻으로, 나이 아흔한 살을 이르는 말.
candidates.check: Translation: 'Mangbaek (望百), noun: meaning to look toward a hundred (百); a word for the age of ninety-one.' The same dictionary defines 망구 (望九), 'looking toward ninety', as the age of 81 (아흔을 바라본다는 뜻으로, 나이 여든한 살을 이르는 말).

candidates.text: The UK had about 114,900 people aged 91 in mid-2024, up from about 79,900 in 2004, official estimates show.

candidates.text: In Japan, 99 is hakuju, ‘white longevity’: take the top stroke, 一 (one), away from 百 (100) and what remains is 白, white.

source.label: Nippon.com, Japanese Names for Age Milestones from 60 to 100, 5 Jan 2024

candidates.evidence: 白寿 ( Hakuju , 99 years old) The kanji for 100 is 百, so take away one top stroke (which also represents the character 一, “one”)—to get 白, which, although it usually means “white,” here represents 99. ... The character 寿, which appears second in this and all subsequent names, means both “congratulations” and “longevity.”
candidates.check: Traditional Japanese milestone name for exactly 99. The Korean Standard Dictionary gives the same derivation for Korean 백수 (白壽): '아흔아홉 살. ‘百’에서 ‘一’을 빼면 99가 되고 ‘白’ 자가 되는 데서 유래한다.'
